title: Chicken Tetrazzini
subtitle: A baked American pasta casserole with chicken, mushrooms, and a creamy sauce
excerpt: Spaghetti and chicken in a sherry-spiked cream sauce, baked under a Parmesan and breadcrumb crust. A mid-century American comfort dish that feeds a crowd.
sourceNotes: Classic American casserole dish, popular from the 1950s onward. Named after opera singer Luisa Tetrazzini. Uses a bechamel-based sauce enriched with cream and sherry.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble the dish and freeze before baking. Thaw overnight in the fridge. Bake from cold, adding 15 minutes to the bake time.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double and bake in two dishes. The sauce scales well.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead, refrigerate covered, and bake when needed.

content.text: Tetrazzini is a baked pasta with a creamy sauce and a crisp topping. Undercook the pasta slightly before it goes in the oven, since it will keep cooking during the bake. The sherry sharpens the sauce without making it taste boozy.
Heat the oven to 190C. Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain and set aside.
Melt 20g of the butter in the frying pan over high heat. Cook the mushrooms for 5 minutes until golden. Season and set aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the large saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the sherry and stir until absorbed. Gradually add the milk and stock, stirring constantly. Cook for 5 minutes until thick and smooth.
Stir in the cream, nutmeg, half the Parmesan, salt, and pepper. Remove from the heat.
Combine the spaghetti, chicken, mushrooms, peas if using, and sauce in the roasting tin. Toss until everything is coated.
Mix the remaining Parmesan with the breadcrumbs and scatter over the top. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The pasta is gluey after baking.
items.cause: The pasta was fully cooked before going in the oven, or the sauce was too thick.
items.fix: Cook pasta 2 minutes short of al dente. Loosen the sauce to a pourable consistency before assembling.

items.symptom: The sauce splits and looks greasy.
items.cause: The oven was too hot or the cream was added to a sauce that was too hot.
items.fix: Stir the cream in off the heat. Keep the oven at 190C, not higher.
Switch to the grill for the final 3 minutes. Watch it closely.
